subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw accept `models.providers.<provider>.enabled?: boolean` as a first-class provider config contract, or should users continue disabling providers through existing model/fallback/allowlist configuration?
rationale: The source proof shows the feature is missing, but AGENTS.md and VISION.md set a high bar for new config keys and provider-routing behavior, so automation should not add this surface without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept provider-level enablement
options.body: Add the config key and require schema, docs, models.json, fallback, catalog, status, and upgrade proof in one bounded implementation.

options.title: Keep existing configuration surfaces
options.body: Close or narrow the request and document the supported provider-disable workaround through model defaults, fallbacks, allowlists, or provider config removal.

options.title: Defer behind broader provider policy
options.body: Keep the issue open as part of a provider-configuration design pass instead of accepting a one-off boolean now.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level enablement
recommendation.body: Add the config key and require schema, docs, models.json, fallback, catalog, status, and upgrade proof in one bounded implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available routing candidate from current-line provenance and the prior Codex review comment on this issue.
